aiExplanation: This function adds up the squares of the numbers sitting at **special positions** in the array, where a position is special if its 1-based index divides the array length evenly. It stores the length in `n`, starts a running total `res` at `0`, and loops over every index `i`. Because JavaScript arrays are 0-based, the 1-based position is `i + 1`, so the check `n % (i + 1) === 0` asks whether that position is a divisor of `n`. When it is, the element is multiplied by itself and added to `res`. After the loop finishes, `res` holds the sum of the squares of all elements at divisor positions and is returned.
